messages:
zoe: seeing a slow creep of pending GPU pods in asia-south1-a. lots of 0.25/0.5 inference tasks scattered, and two 8GPU jobs stuck pending

rahul: is this the usual anchor ttl/warmpool tango?

zoe: not exactly. scheduler traces show an affinity hysteresis: when a family previously filled a node, we bias future small pods to avoid moving them (hysteresis window=30m). combined with high-weight prefer-label hints, the scheduler spray places small pods across nodes rather than packing contiguous slots

maria: can you share a pod and node snapshot?

zoe: pod excerpt:
```
Name: infer-sample-204
requests.nvidia.com/gpu: 0.5
annotations: redwood/scheduler-hint=prefer-fast-net
Status: Pending (0/40 nodes fit: Insufficient contiguous gpus)
```

node snapshot (sanitized):
```
node-a: 8 free contiguous (anchor=family-alpha, last_used=50m)
node-b: many 0.5s scattered
node-c: 4 free contiguous
```

infra-bot: [alert] fragmentation_warning asia-south1-a unusable_gpus=24 anomaly=0.61 triggered=1768660022

oncall: please confirm whether we should revoke stale anchors or run a targeted coalescer

rahul: two safe actions: 1) lower prefer-fast-net hint weight from 0.8->0.35 for this rollout 2) run defrag dry-run filtering fractional pods only

zoe: running dry-run: `infractl defrag --region asia-south1-a --filter "requests.gpu<=0.5" --dry-run`

(micropause)

zoe: dry-run: would move 12 pods, free 2x8 contiguous slots, let 2 blocked 8GPU jobs schedule. recommends dont-evict-age<4m and max-evict=15%

maria: approved conservative execute. also lower anchor-hysteresis window from 30m->8m for non-critical families in scheduler config as a follow-up

infra-bot: [note] defrag job df-1201 executed; moved 10 pods; freed 2x8 slots; pending dropped from 9->3 at 1768660075

rahul: created INFRA-9001: "affinity-hysteresis-causes-fractional-spray". action items: add fragmentation metric to canary dashboards, make hint weight rollout-guarded, add TTL/hysteresis guardrails. Assigning to eng-scheduler

zoe: cluster stabilized, two big jobs scheduled. closing unless anyone sees new spikes. :white_check_mark:
